title: AI for Beginners: Where to Start (No Tech Skills Needed)
style: Read this like a friendly, confident teacher explaining to a small business owner. Warm, clear, unhurried, natural pauses.

segments.title:
Everyone says "use AI."
But where do you start?
segments.say: Everyone keeps telling you to use AI. Your friends, the news, maybe even your customers. But nobody tells you where to actually start. If you run a business, or you just want an easier week, this video is for you. In the next few minutes, you'll set up your first AI assistant, write your first prompts, and leave with a ten-minute daily plan. No tech skills needed.

segments.title: A helper you talk to in plain English
bullets: It reads, writes, summarizes and explains
You type (or talk) like you would to a person
It works in seconds, any time of day
segments.say: First, what are we even talking about? An AI assistant is a helper you talk to in plain English. You type, or even speak, the way you'd talk to a smart assistant sitting next to you. It can read, write, summarize, explain and organize. And it does it in seconds, any time of day.

segments.title: Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini
bullets: All three have a free version
Pick one and stick with it for 30 days
On this channel we use Claude
segments.say: There are three big names you'll hear: Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini. All three have a free version, and all three are good. The biggest mistake beginners make is jumping between tools. So pick one, and stick with it for thirty days. On this channel, we use Claude, because it writes clearly and it can connect to tools you already use. But everything you learn here works in the others too.

segments.title: The prompt formula
bullets: WHO: "Act as my customer service manager"
WHAT: "Write a reply to this customer"
DETAILS: who it's for, the facts, the tone
FORMAT: "Short, friendly, 3 sentences"
segments.say: Step two. Learn one simple formula for asking. Who, what, details, format. Who: tell it what role to play, like, act as my customer service manager. What: tell it the job, like, write a reply to this customer. Details: give it the facts and the tone you want. And format: say how you want it back, like, short and friendly, three sentences. That's it. Better details in, better answers out.

chat.user: Act as my customer service manager. Write a reply to a customer asking when their order will arrive. Friendly, 3 sentences.
chat.ai: Hi Sarah, thanks so much for checking in! Your order is scheduled to arrive this Thursday between 10 AM and 2 PM. We'll text you when the driver is 30 minutes away. Let me know if anything changes!

segments.title: A delayed delivery email
bullets: "Act as a friendly store manager."
"Write an email to a customer whose sofa delivery is delayed one week."
"Apologize, give the new date, offer free delivery."
"Keep it under 100 words."
segments.say: Let's try it. Imagine you run a furniture store, and a customer's sofa delivery is delayed a week. You type: act as a friendly store manager. Write an email to a customer whose sofa delivery is delayed one week. Apologize, give the new date, and offer free delivery. Keep it under one hundred words. In about five seconds, you have a calm, professional email that would have taken you fifteen minutes to write while stressed.

chat.user: Act as a friendly store manager. Write an email to a customer whose sofa delivery is delayed one week. Apologize, give the new date, offer free delivery. Under 100 words.
chat.ai:
Hi James,
I'm sorry to share that your sofa delivery is delayed by one week. Your new delivery date is Friday, March 14. To make up for the wait, your delivery is on us, free of charge. Thank you for your patience. We know you're excited to enjoy your new sofa!
Warm regards, Dana

segments.title: A week of meals on a budget
bullets: "Plan 5 dinners for a family of 4."
"Budget: $100 for the week."
"Give me one grocery list grouped by store aisle."
segments.say: It works for your personal life too. Try this: plan five dinners for a family of four. My budget is one hundred dollars for the week. Give me one grocery list grouped by store aisle. You get a meal plan and a shopping list you can take straight to the store. That's real time and real money saved, every single week.

segments.title: Understand any document
bullets: Upload a bill, lease or contract (PDF or photo)
"Explain this in plain English."
"What fees or deadlines should I watch for?"
segments.say: Example three. Paperwork. You can upload a bill, a lease, or a contract, as a PDF or even a photo from your phone. Then ask: explain this in plain English. What fees or deadlines should I watch for? It's like having someone patient read the fine print with you.

chat.user: [Electric bill.pdf]  Explain this in plain English. What fees or deadlines should I watch for?
chat.ai:
In short: you used more power than last month, so your bill went up $18.
• Due date: the 21st. After that, a $10 late fee applies.
• 'Fuel adjustment' is a pass-through cost, not an error.
• Tip: you qualify for budget billing to even out your payments.

segments.title: Have a conversation, not one question
bullets: "Make it shorter."
"Make it friendlier."
"Give me three other versions."
"What did I forget?"
segments.say: Step three. This is the secret most people miss. Don't stop after the first answer. Talk back to it. Say, make it shorter. Make it friendlier. Give me three other versions. Or my favorite: what did I forget? The second and third answers are usually much better than the first.

chat.ai: Hi James! Quick heads-up: your sofa is coming a week later, on Friday, March 14. Sorry for the wait. Delivery is free on us! 😊 Dana

segments.title: What NOT to do
bullets: Never paste passwords, card numbers or Social Security numbers
Don't share customers' private information
Double-check facts, prices and numbers
For legal, tax or medical: ask a professional
segments.say: Now, a few rules to stay safe. Never paste passwords, card numbers, or Social Security numbers. Don't share your customers' private information. AI can make mistakes, so double check facts, prices and numbers before you send anything. And for legal, tax or medical decisions, use AI to prepare your questions, then ask a professional.

segments.title: One small business: about $480 a month saved
bullets: Asked AI to review every subscription and ad
Paused ads that brought very few real customers
Cancelled a tool nobody used
Results vary. The method works for anyone
segments.say: Does this actually save money? Here's a real example. A small installation business asked AI to review every subscription and every ad it was paying for. It paused ads that were bringing very few real customers, and cancelled a tool nobody was using. The result: about four hundred eighty dollars a month saved. Your results will be different, but the method works for anyone. We'll show you exactly how in a future video.

segments.title: 10 minutes a day
bullets: Day 1: Rewrite one email you'd normally send
Day 2: Plan your week
Day 3: Summarize a long document
Day 4: Write a social media post
Day 5: Plan meals and a grocery list
Day 6: Ask it to explain something you never understood
Day 7: Ask "how could AI save me time?"
segments.say: So here's your challenge. Ten minutes a day, for seven days. Day one: rewrite one email you'd normally send. Day two: plan your week. Day three: summarize a long document. Day four: write a social media post. Day five: plan meals and a grocery list. Day six: ask it to explain something you never quite understood. And day seven: ask it, here's what my week looks like, how could AI save me time? Tell me in the comments how it goes. We'll feature the best results in a future video.
